name: British Countryside
periodStart: Practices from Medieval times, visuals from Victorian era
summary: British Countryside (or British Sportsmanship , English/Scottish Countryside ) describes the subculture of sports played by the nobility of Britain in their manors in rural areas, as well as some employees of the estate.
description:
British Countryside (or British Sportsmanship , English/Scottish Countryside ) describes the subculture of sports played by the nobility of Britain in their manors in rural areas, as well as some employees of the estate. It includes hunting, shooting, and equestrian sports, which are specialized, with many traditions and forms of dress associated with these activities.

The nobles in Britain historically owned estates, with large swaths of land and forest. After spending time in London for social and political reasons, they would go back to the manor and the men would often go out on hunting excursions and ride horses, particularly in autumn, which is hunting season. The nobles also hired employees with specialized skills, such as gamekeepers and stablehands, who would also participate in hunting and equestrianism in order to maintain the estate and aid the nobles.

From the Victorian era to the 1950s, the visual culture for this aesthetic developed, with the clothing largely being developed during this time. However, the aesthetic has become less common, as fox hunting has been banned in many parts of the UK since the 2000s and the British nobility take on more modern practices and hobbies.

Many of these visuals are a large basis of the Preppy aesthetic, and interior and fashion designers often specifically create rooms, garments, etc. themed after this culture. The visual culture is also important to the conceptualization of rural Britain, with this aesthetic largely being featured in period dramas and nostalgic art.
culturalContext: Key values (per the Aesthetics Wiki): Competition, wealth, pride, tradition, masculinity

visualDNA.colour: Brown, dark green, red, olive, beige

fashion.Tops: Tweed sports coats, which are tweed blazers that allow for more mobility.; Knitted sweaters.
fashion.Shoes: Wellington boots; Leather men's dress shoes
fashion.Accessories: Flat cap: It protects the head from drizzle and retains heat well.; Wool scarves: Must be tartan or solid colors in deep, natural tones. Often made of cashmere or fine sheep’s wool.; Silk neckerchiefs: Men can wear them under a shirt as an ascot.

graphicDesign.Overview: The British Countryside design style is based on a balance between historic charm, practicality, and a close connection to nature. Unlike minimalist contemporary styles, it values a lived-in feel, the functionality of every detail, and the use of natural materials.
graphicDesign.England: Wood and stone: Floors made of solid wood planks or natural stone are durable and practical for country living.
graphicDesign.Scotland: Scottish interiors are built around rugged textures that can withstand the cold climate.
graphicDesign.Functional zones and elements: Fireplace: The central element of the living room, providing warmth and coziness.
graphicDesign.Furniture and decor: Comfort: Deep, plush armchairs and low-slung sofas.
graphicDesign.Golf: Playing golf in the British countryside is a true delight of cultural heritage.
